current_example.title: Example: Finding a Marginal Distribution From a Joint Distribution: Non-Rectangular Domains

q-142751.name: Question 1
q-142751.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\pi }\,\operatorname{sin}⁡y, & 0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{2}, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expression for the marginal PDF ${f}_{X}(x).$
q-142751.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $X$ for $0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2}$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{2}{\pi }\,\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }[-\operatorname{cos}⁡y]_{y=0}^{y=\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }(-\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}+\operatorname{cos}⁡0) \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{X}(x)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\pi }, & 0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2}, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-110408.name: Question 2
q-110408.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}{y}^{2}, & 0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expression for the marginal PDF ${f}_{X}(x).$
q-110408.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $X$ for $0\le x\le 2$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[{y}^{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({1}^{3}-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{X}(x)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}, & 0\le x\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-142815.name: Question 3
q-142815.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{-(x+y)}, & x\ge 0,\,y\ge 0, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expression for the marginal PDF ${f}_{X}(x).$
q-142815.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $X$ for $x\ge 0$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-(x+y)}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[-{e}^{-(x+y)}]}_{y=0}^{y=\infty } \\  & =(0+{e}^{-(x+0)}) \\  & ={e}^{-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{X}(x)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{-x}, & x\ge 0, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-142870.name: Question 4
q-142870.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}-1}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y), & 0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{4},\,0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{4}, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expression for the marginal PDF ${f}_{Y}(y).$
q-142870.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $Y$ for $0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{4}$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}-1}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}-1}[-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)]_{x=0}^{x=\pi /4} \\  & =\frac{1}{1-\sqrt{2}}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)]_{x=0}^{x=\pi /4} \\  & =\frac{1}{1-\sqrt{2}}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}+y)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0+y)] \\  & =\frac{1}{1-\sqrt{2}}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}+y)-\operatorname{cos}⁡y).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{1-\sqrt{2}}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}+y)-\operatorname{cos}⁡y), & 0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{4}, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let X and Y be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function f(x,y)={12−1sin⁡(x+y),0≤x≤π4,0≤y≤π4,0,otherwise. Find the expression for the marginal PDF fY(y).

a
fY(y)={11−2(sin⁡y−cos⁡y),0≤y≤π4,0,otherwise.
b
fY(y)={11−2(cos⁡(π4+y)−cos⁡y),0≤y≤π4,0,otherwise.
c
fY(y)={11−2(sin⁡y+cos⁡y),0≤y≤π4,0,otherwise.
d
fY(y)={11−2(sin⁡y−sin⁡(π4+y)),0≤y≤π4,0,otherwise.
e
fY(y)={11−2(sin⁡(π4+y)−sin⁡y),0≤y≤π4,0,otherwise.
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

If X and Y are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function f(x,y), then the marginal density functions for X and Y are

fX(x)=∫−∞∞f(x,y)dy,fY(y)=∫−∞∞f(x,y)dx.

In our case, the marginal density function of Y for 0≤y≤π4 is

fY(y)=∫0π/412−1sin⁡(x+y)dx=12−1[−cos⁡(x+y)]x=0x=π/4=11−2[cos⁡(x+y)]x=0x=π/4=11−2[cos⁡(π4+y)−cos⁡(0+y)]=11−2(cos⁡(π4+y)−cos⁡y).

Therefore, the full expression for fY(y) is given by

fY(y)={11−2(cos⁡(π4+y)−cos⁡y),0≤y≤π4,0,otherwise.

q-142886.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{-(\frac{x}{3}+3y)}, & x\ge 0,\,y\ge 0, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expression for the marginal PDF ${f}_{Y}(y).$
q-142886.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $Y$ for $y\ge 0$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-(\frac{x}{3}+3y)}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[-3{e}^{-(\frac{x}{3}+3y)}]}_{x=0}^{x=\infty } \\  & =-3{[{e}^{-(\frac{x}{3}+3y)}]}_{x=0}^{x=\infty } \\  & =-3[0-{e}^{-(0+3y)}] \\  & =3{e}^{-3y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}3{e}^{-3y}, & y\ge 0, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-110416.name: Question 6
q-110416.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{6}(x+y), & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 3, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(Y\le 1).$
q-110416.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $Y$ for $0\le y\le 3$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{6}(x+y)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+xy]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\frac{1}{2}+y]-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{12}+\frac{y}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{12}+\frac{y}{6}, & 0\le y\le 3, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\le 1) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{1}{f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{1}{12}+\frac{y}{6})\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{y}{12}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{12}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =[\frac{1}{12}+\frac{1}{12}]-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-142963.name: Question 10
q-142963.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{16}({x}^{3}+{y}^{3}), & 0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(Y\ge 1).$
q-142963.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $Y$ for $0\le y\le 2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{16}({x}^{3}+{y}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{[\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}+x{y}^{3}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =\frac{1}{16}[\frac{{2}^{4}}{4}+(2){y}^{3}]-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{16}(4+2{y}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{8}{y}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{8}{y}^{3}, & 0\le y\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\ge 1) & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }{f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{8}{y}^{3})\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{1}{4}y+\frac{1}{32}{y}^{4}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =[\frac{1}{4}(2)+\frac{1}{32}{2}^{4}]-[\frac{1}{4}(1)+\frac{1}{32}{1}^{4}] \\  & =1-\frac{9}{32} \\  & =\frac{23}{32}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-142855.name: Question 11
q-142855.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with a joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\frac{3x}{2({y}^{2}+1)},\,{y}^{2}\le x\le 1.
$$

Find the expression for the marginal PDF ${f}_{Y}(y).$
q-142855.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's sketch the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,{y}^{2}\le x\le 1\}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14272472/assets/cf0c8438253a5b46a468610ca62bc17a9ce927c98045eb461291d98644241e2f.png)

In our case, the marginal density function of $Y$ for $-1\le y\le 1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{{y}^{2}}^{1}\frac{3x}{2({y}^{2}+1)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2({y}^{2}+1)}{\int }_{{y}^{2}}^{1}x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2({y}^{2}+1)}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{x={y}^{2}}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{3}{4({y}^{2}+1)}[1-{({y}^{2})}^{2}] \\  & =\frac{3}{4({y}^{2}+1)}[1-{y}^{4}] \\  & =\frac{3(1-{y}^{2})(1+{y}^{2})}{4({y}^{2}+1)} \\  & =\frac{3(1-{y}^{2})}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3(1-{y}^{2})}{4}, & -1\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
